newsitem.title: DENMARK: Profit-taking damps Danish bond prices rise.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking damps Danish bond prices rise.

text.p: Profit-taking by foreign investors, combined with central bank bond sales, put the brake on prices on Tuesday afternoon after the morning had seen the 10-year benchmark heading for a new record, dealers said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 closed at 112.71, yielding 6.12 percent, up from Monday's 112.68 but off the day's high of 113.08 and short of the February 14 closing high of 112.81.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened to 66 basis points from an earlier 63 bp. The benchmark's March future rose 0.50 point, to 112.62, with 32 contracts traded.

"It is mainly profit-taking from foreign investors and the National Bank's sale of paper that has pressed the Danish market," a dealer said, adding that the bank sold about 0.5 billion crowns worth of five percent 2005 and seven percent 2007 bonds.
He expected a hesitant market on Wednesday morning, ahead of U.S. consumer prices and trade balance data due at 1330 GMT.

The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 closed on Tuesday up 0.15 point to 90.50. The crown traded at 3.8155 per mark, weakening from around 3.8120 at the opening. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969650
